**Ticket:** `docs/tickets/274_P35.15a__technology-typing-slug-and-facets.md` (manifest row 274) · **Base:** `r11/P35.14b-entity-typing-and-hosted-check` (`8b35cca9`) · **Branch:** `r11/P35.15a-technology-typing-slug-and-facets` · **OM-20 posture:** **pre-authorised** — the GATE-G4 11B OM-20 list names P35.15a verbatim and the operator approved all 19 (2026-10-09T17:32Z; expiry: next sub-round gate). The write itself is **paused by the AR-3 freeze** (no hosted write before 2026-10-13 12:00Z) and queues in RETURN PASS per OM-19.

## Why

Every camera-registry subject was emitted `record_kind="traffic_camera"` with no technology predicate — an ALPR reader, a police CCTV, and a traffic-management camera were publicly indistinguishable (F-329). Worse, ER compatibility relied on source-name substrings (NEW-7/FM-05): the largest ALPR group classed as traffic cameras. The fix is declared, not inferred: each `camera_registry_targets.toml`/`dot_511_targets.toml` target declares its SKOS technology slug, validated against `ontology/vocab/technology.yaml`.

Subject identity is deliberately unchanged (`traffic_camera:<src>:<tgt>:<ref>`) — re-scheming to `alpr-fixed:…` would fork every existing identity in an append-only store. The declared technology travels as the entity row's record_kind, a `technology` claim (the spine-measurable signal — the sink skips non-claim records), resolution metadata, and the export/web field. The ~200k-subject backfill is **P35.15b**, explicitly out of scope here.

## What ships

- **Target slugs:** all 274 camera-class targets carry an active-member `technology` slug (`alpr-fixed/-mobile/-trailer`, `fixed-camera-ptz/-cctv/-unspecified`, `camera-trailer-video/-unspecified`, `private-camera-integration-live-feeds`, `uas-general`, …); optional `record_kind` may declare `traffic_camera` only on a surveillance-video-domain target.
- **`dot_511.py`:** `technology_slugs()` loads active members via `ontology.generate.load_vocab` (no second allowlist); `assert_target_technology` fails the run (never a per-record rejection — a broken target is a config defect) on missing/retired/unknown slugs; `CameraRegistryEntry.technology`/`record_kind` propagate through target expansion; every subject emits a `technology` claim plus the entity row with the declared subtype.
- **`dot_511_vocab` 2026.10.11.1:** `technology` joins the predicate allowlist; `sig-connectors validate` runs `target_technology_violations` (membership + record-kind compat over every camera target).
- **Resolution `camera-sites/1.2.0`, rules `3.1-interim`:** `CameraRecord.technology` + `declared_technologies` (multi-cardinality); `device_class` resolves the declared slug via the new `[[classes.technology_rule]]` table first — substring rules survive only for undeclared (pre-backfill) records and as the audit arm (`declared_substring_mismatch`, `multiple_declared_technologies` findings; class feeds the existing `incompatible` pair block); run keys digest every record field; pair evidence carries the declared slugs; the PG seam reads `technology` claims (`CAMERA_PREDICATES` + a DISTINCT multi-value query).
- **Exports:** the `technology` predicate joins shaping; `ShapedSite.technology` → the sites/`map` export column (the field `release.py` already carried now populates); `PublishedRecord` gains `technology = {id, basis}` with honest basis (`declared_technology_claim`/`conflicted`/`unreported`) — projection **sig.published-record/2**; dossier pages render the row.
- **Web:** `MapAsset.technology`, a Technology column + facet band on `/map/`, fixtures spanning multiple classes.
